extracted.intended_audience: researchers and scientists seeking funding or engagement with Breakthrough T1D (JDRF) for type 1 diabetes research
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational guidance from Breakthrough T1D describing research priorities and programmatic focus areas for funding, spanning basic science through clinical trials aimed at curing type 1 diabetes and improving quality of life. Useful for researchers planning grant proposals or aligning projects with the funder's strategic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall mission: cure and improve lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Curing T1D. Improving Lives. We propel research—from basic science to clinical trials—in key therapy areas to improve lives and drive toward cures for type 1 diabetes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breakthrough T1D funds projects across the research continuum with the dual aims of developing cures (restoring insulin independence and stopping autoimmunity) and improving everyday life for people living with T1D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing goal: restore insulin production and stop autoimmunity
rubrics_metrics.description: To make cures a reality we need to restore the body’s ability to make insulin and turn off the autoimmune attack responsible for destroying the beta cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded research should aim at mechanisms and interventions that either restore endogenous insulin production or halt/modify the autoimmune process that destroys beta cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cures portfolio — Early Detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a global universal T1D early detection strategy to identify high-risk individuals, reduce diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) at diagnosis, and speed up the development of disease-modifying therapies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that create scalable early-detection approaches, risk-stratification tools, or programs reducing DKA at diagnosis are priorities because early identification accelerates intervention and therapy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cures portfolio — Disease-Modifying Therapies
rubrics_metrics.description: Powering the research and development of new therapies that can slow, halt, or reverse the course of T1D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority given to interventions with potential to change disease trajectory (not only symptomatic control), including preclinical and clinical studies targeting immune modulation, beta-cell preservation, or other disease-altering mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cures portfolio — Cell Therapies
rubrics_metrics.description: Investing in research and clinical trials to develop life-changing therapies that insert healthy insulin-producing cells into people with T1D with minimal or no immunosuppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for approaches that provide durable beta-cell replacement or regeneration while minimizing the need for chronic immunosuppression (e.g., encapsulation, immune-evasive cells, local immune control). Clinical trial development in this area is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving lives portfolio — Drugs and devices for glucose control
rubrics_metrics.description: Making T1D easier to manage with improved technology, insulins, and other drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects improving glycemic management via novel insulins, delivery systems, closed-loop/artificial pancreas technologies, sensors, and other devices or pharmacologic adjuncts that reduce burden and improve outcomes are within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving lives portfolio — Complications and behavioral health therapies
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovering therapies that intervene in heart, eye, and kidney disease and reducing the mental burden of T1D through research and clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research addressing prevention or treatment of T1D complications (cardiovascular, retinopathy, nephropathy) and interventions for mental health or behavioral burden associated with T1D are priority areas; clinical trial support is highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research continuum emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakthrough T1D is focused on the entire T1D continuum, from those who don’t have T1D to those who have lived with it for decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded work may span basic discovery, translational research, and clinical trials; proposals should situate projects within this continuum and explain how they advance from discovery toward tangible patient benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials are critical
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical trials advance care so people living with T1D can live fuller, healthier lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization emphasizes supporting clinical development and trial activity as an essential pathway to bring therapies to patients; proposals that enable or accelerate trials (e.g., infrastructure, endpoints, trial design) are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding opportunities and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakthrough T1D offers a wide variety of grants and fellowships to researchers. All qualified scientists are encouraged to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should consult the funder's funding opportunities page for specific grant types, eligibility criteria, and application details; the organization supports diverse investigators and career stages through multiple award mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and portfolio tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Search our abstract database for past research funding information, or see where Breakthrough T1D’s nearly 500 active grants are driving progress today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can use the public abstract database to align proposals with prior and active awards, identify gaps, and avoid duplication; reviewers and applicants can assess portfolio focus areas via these resources.
